root_cause.text: In `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()` in `net/sunrpc/xprtrdma/svc_rdma_rw.c`, the code used `head->rc_curpage` (the page index) as the byte offset into the destination page for `memcpy()`, so inline RDMA data could be copied to the wrong location instead of within the current page.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `memcpy(dst + head->rc_curpage, src + offset, page_len);` to `memcpy((unsigned char *)dst + head->rc_pageoff, src + offset, page_len);`, and the commit message explicitly says it “added rc_curpage (page index) to the page base instead of the byte offset rc_pageoff” and that `rc_pageoff` should be used so copies “land within the current page.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the inline RDMA copy to use the current page offset when writing data into the destination page.
intent_record.what: In `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range()`, the destination pointer used in `memcpy()` was changed from `dst + head->rc_curpage` to `((unsigned char *)dst + head->rc_pageoff)`, while the copied length and subsequent accounting code remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: This makes the inline copy write into the current page at the correct byte offset within that page, instead of using the current page index as a pointer offset. At runtime, it prevents data from being copied to the wrong memory location and fixes corruption or incorrect placement of RDMA inline payload data.
